question: Can run 004 and 007's recipe paint the lighthouse top for chapter 1's new opening spread, a night sky that makes the shore feel like a new place, and the lamp's wick?
why: Owner, headset session 1: open with the lit lamp and its beam, then it goes out and the chapter is the journey to relight it; the spreads felt static because they shared one sky and headland. The opening spread needs the lighthouse up close; the shore needs its own sky; the story needs the lamp's lost wick.
sameAcrossJobs: seedream5_pro, run 004's set wording and 007's piece wording, flat vivid magenta paper with a margin for cut pieces. The key and ground are full-bleed and aren't cut. Layers are placed on run 004's 2720 px canvas at its set density.
decideBy: Every cut piece passes run 004's and 006's checks: paper border, one piece, magenta residue, at least 97% of paint kept.
The lamp room's glass can be recolored gold for the lit lamp with its alpha unchanged, as run 007's lamp.
The owner judges the spreads in the headset.
learnEvenIfRejected: Whether a close-up of an existing set's landmark keeps the book's style, and whether a time-of-day repaint of a layer keeps its shape.
reusableOutput: The lamp spread (sky, lamp room, railings, gallery floor) and its lit lamp, the shore's night sky, and the lamp-wick object.
capNote: Owner's cap for art while away: 120 credits. Key 5, six 2K layers 54, wick sheet 5. Contingency for repaints.

jobs.prompt: A wide picture in exactly the painting style and colors of Figure 1, with no characters: the very top of the same old stone lighthouse, seen up close from its own gallery. In the left third stands the round lamp room: tall glass panes in a dark iron frame, a domed copper roof with a small weather vane, and inside it a big brass lamp with a large clear glass lens, dark and unlit. A narrow stone walkway runs around it with a low iron railing at its outer edge. Beyond the railing, far below, a calm sea and the distant curve of the shore at gentle early dusk, and a wide soft dusk-blue sky with a few long clouds. The right half of the walkway is open and calm, for small characters to stand on. Mid-to-high values, never dark, no night. No light sources, no beams, no lit windows, no directional cast shadows. Hand-painted traditional watercolor with a fine graphite pencil outline, from a vintage natural history picture book. Soft pigment washes, visible paper grain, gentle edges. No text.

Figure 1 is the composed scene. Paint only the sky and the far sea from Figure 1, as a single die-cut paper stage piece, flat-on, in exactly the same painting style and colors. A wide band of soft dusk-blue sky with a few long clouds, and along its lower edge a thin strip of calm distant sea with the faint curve of a far shore, as seen from high up. Its top edge is cut in soft rolling cloud shapes. Its silhouette has a clean hard edge traced with a fine pencil line, and a perfectly straight flat bottom edge. Leave a wide margin of empty paper on all four sides, with nothing touching the edge of the image. Paint the whole piece continuously, including every part that other pieces would normally hide, right down to its straight bottom edge, with no gaps or holes. Pale, gentle dusk values. No lighthouse, no lit windows, no beams. Hand-painted traditional watercolor with a fine graphite pencil outline, from a vintage natural history picture book. Soft pigment washes, visible paper grain, gentle edges. On plain flat solid vivid magenta paper, one even color. No pink or purple in the painting. No text.
